paragraphs: Every London borough runs its own fostering service, and many now recruit together. In May 2024 fourteen boroughs combined their recruitment for the first time: Waltham Forest, Barking and Dagenham, Havering, Newham, Redbridge and Tower Hamlets as Local Community Fostering in the north-east, and Brent, Ealing, Hammersmith and Fulham, Harrow, Hillingdon, Hounslow, Kensington and Chelsea and Westminster as Foster with West London. In the north, Barnet, Camden, Enfield, Hackney, Haringey and Islington have worked together since 2012 and now share a fostering hub hosted by Camden. Alongside the councils, independent agencies such as those listed below approve and support carers across the capital.

The need is real. When the fourteen boroughs launched, Tower Hamlets said there were four London children needing a foster home for every approved carer, and that the number of approved fostering households had fallen from 3,685 in 2014 to 2,560 at the end of March 2023. Ofsted figures reported in December 2024 showed 5,130 London households enquiring about fostering in a year, but only 355 applications. The west London partnership says it especially needs carers for teenagers, brothers and sisters who want to stay together, babies, children from diverse ethnic backgrounds and children with special educational needs or disabilities.

Space is often the hurdle in London: children aged two and over need their own bedroom, and a third of people asked in the boroughs' 2024 survey said they did not have the room. If you do, talk to your own borough and to two or three of the agencies below, and compare their training, support and pay before you choose.
